clue.text: Behind teacher's back, young delinquent talked a lot

indicators.note: behind tells us the delinquent's word is placed after the teacher's word

parts.note: a rabbi is a Jewish religious teacher; back says the next piece goes at its rear
a Ted, or Teddy boy, was a 1950s British youth often seen as a hooligan

explanation.surface: A young offender chatters away while the teacher's back is turned.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind teacher's back' reads as the classroom idiom, but it places TED at the back of RABBI. A Teddy boy (TED) was a 1950s British youth-culture figure associated with delinquency.
explanation.definitionFit: To rabbit (on) is British slang for chattering at length, so the past tense means went on and on.

clue.text: Whitehall endeavouring to give asylum to former president

indicators.note: giving asylum means sheltering someone within, so the run of letters sits inside the words Whitehall endeavouring

explanation.surface: The British government is trying to offer refuge to an ousted head of state.
explanation.walkthrough: Whitehall is the street of British government offices, standing for the government itself; here it only supplies letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Salvador Allende was President of Chile from 1970 until the 1973 coup.

clue.text: Be one over the eight, guzzling order for liqueur

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: guzzling means swallowing greedily, so the order is taken inside the number

parts.note: nine is one more than eight
an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: Someone tipsy, knocking back drinks, orders a liqueur.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One over the eight' is a British idiom for slightly drunk, but here it is plain arithmetic; 'guzzling' puts the order inside the number.
explanation.definitionFit: Bénédictine is a French herbal liqueur, originally linked with Benedictine monks.

clue.text: For example, Mr right (that sportswoman's after?)

explanation.surface: A clue musing on Mr Right and what a sportswoman pursues.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Right is the ideal partner a woman seeks, but the clue splits it: Mr is a form of address, a right (as in a legal claim) is another sense, and a sportswoman chases a championship.
explanation.definitionFit: Mr is an honorific; a legal claim to property is called this; and a championship is what a competitor strives to win.

clue.text: Falsely claimed to make a sort of point

indicators.note: falsely suggests something not genuine, so the letters of claimed are rearranged

explanation.surface: A false claim is made to score a point.
explanation.definitionFit: A decimal point separates the whole number from the fractional part.

clue.text: Brandy before hike is fine

indicators.note: before tells us the fine letter comes ahead of the hike word

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencil leads
a hike in prices is a raise

explanation.surface: Having a brandy before a long walk is perfectly fine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hike' suggests a country walk, but here it is an increase.
explanation.definitionFit: Fraise is a French eau de vie distilled from strawberries, a kind of fruit brandy.

clue.text: Lively dance stirred up an old fear

indicators.note: stirring up agitates and mixes, so the letters of an old fear are rearranged

explanation.surface: A frantic dance rouses an ancient dread.
explanation.definitionFit: The farandole is a lively Provençal chain dance performed with linked hands.

clue.text: Girl with a new name

explanation.surface: A girl takes on a new name.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name, so a crossword example of a girl.

clue.text: Crew member serving dish with meat — tough, not hot?

parts.note: a stew is a slow-cooked dish usually containing meat

indicators.note: not says the hot letter is left out of the tough word

parts.note: hard means tough
H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: An airline attendant serves a meat stew and asks whether it is tough but not hot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not hot' sounds like a complaint about the food, but it removes H from HARD, leaving ARD.
explanation.definitionFit: A steward is an attendant on a ship or aircraft who looks after passengers.

clue.text: Extremist group, wild frantic one restrained in sudden attack?

indicators.note: restrained in means held within, so the scrambled letters go inside the attack word

parts.note: a lunge is a sudden forward thrust

indicators.note: wild means out of control, so the letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A wild, frenzied person is held back during a sudden charge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wild' scrambles the letters of frantic together with I into ATICFRIN; 'restrained in' sets that run inside the attack word.
explanation.definitionFit: The lunatic fringe is the most extreme minority within a political or social movement.

clue.text: Tense individual seen with dagger every now and then

parts.note: one means a single individual

indicators.note: every now and then means at intervals, so only alternate letters of dagger are taken

explanation.surface: A lone figure is spotted carrying a knife from time to time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Every now and then' takes the 1st, 3rd and 5th letters of dagger: D, G, E.
explanation.definitionFit: Being on edge is an idiom for being nervous and jumpy.

clue.text: This person extremely slow, restricted by tight clothes

parts.note: this person is the setter, who calls themself me

indicators.note: restricted by means hemmed in, so the selected letters go inside the stingy word

parts.note: near is an old word for tight-fisted, stingy

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes, the first and last letters, of slow

explanation.surface: The setter moves very slowly, hampered by a tight outfit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tight' means stingy, not snug-fitting; 'extremely' takes the first and last letters of slow, which go inside the stingy word.
explanation.definitionFit: Menswear is a retail category of garments for males.

clue.text: We ultimately appreciated sounds of bells band produced

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the final letter of appreciated is used

parts.note: ding is the sound of a bell struck once
ring is the sound a bell makes

explanation.surface: We enjoyed the pealing of bells that a musical group produced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Band' looks like musicians but it is a ring worn on the finger; 'sounds of bells' gives two words, DING and RING.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain gold band is the usual form of the ring exchanged at a marriage ceremony.

clue.text: Rogue and I will get together after brief kiss, finding love? Wrong

indicators.note: after tells us the rogue and the rest follow the shortened kiss
brief means cut short, so the kiss word loses its final letter

parts.note: a peck is a quick kiss
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue
I'll is the contraction of I will
love is zero in tennis, written O

explanation.surface: A rascal plans to meet someone after a quick kiss, seeking romance that goes wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brief' trims PECK to PEC; 'love' is the tennis score nil, O.
explanation.definitionFit: A peccadillo is a small sin or minor fault.

clue.text: Word once coined to describe minute plumbing fitment

indicators.note: to describe here means to draw a line round, so the scrambled letters enclose the minute letter
coined means newly invented, so the letters of word once are made into something new

explanation.surface: A term invented long ago names a tiny piece of plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Minute' looks like tiny but it is M; 'to describe' means to draw around, so the anagram of WORD ONCE encloses M.
explanation.definitionFit: A downcomer is a vertical pipe carrying water or gas downward, such as a downpipe.

clue.text: Confident fellow finally overcome by failure

parts.note: a dud is something that fails to work

indicators.note: finally means at the end, so only the last letter of overcome is used

explanation.surface: A self-assured man is at last beaten by a flop.
explanation.definitionFit: A dude is an informal word for a man, especially a cool, self-assured one.

clue.text: Language teaching hasn't always impressed heads

indicators.note: heads means the leading letters, so the first letter of each of the four words is taken

explanation.surface: Teaching a language has not always impressed head teachers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heads' suggests head teachers, but it means the first letters of the four words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Thai is the official language of Thailand.

clue.text: Female outlaw having drug as source of poison

parts.note: a hen is a female bird
to outlaw something is to ban it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: A female bandit uses a narcotic as her poison.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outlaw' reads as a bandit but it is the verb, to ban.
explanation.definitionFit: Henbane is a toxic plant of the nightshade family, used historically as a poison.

clue.text: Travels in group in western mountain range

indicators.note: in tells us the group word sits inside the mountain range

parts.note: the Andes are the South American mountain range
a ring is a group, as in a spy ring

explanation.surface: Journeys with a party through mountains in the west.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Group' is meant as in a smuggling ring; the second 'in' places the group inside the South American mountains.
explanation.definitionFit: Wanderings are journeys or roamings from place to place.

clue.text: Put heads together to make vegetarian dish

parts.note: nut is slang for the head
loaf is slang for the head, as in use your loaf

explanation.surface: Put your heads together and cook a meatless meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put heads together' sounds like brainstorming, but it joins two slang words for the head: NUT and LOAF ('use your loaf' is British slang for think).
explanation.definitionFit: A nut loaf is a baked dish of chopped nuts and vegetables eaten as a meat substitute.

clue.text: French author's written about river close to aquitaine area

indicators.note: written about means written around, so the author's name is set around the river letters

parts.note: André Gide was a French novelist
on can mean close to, as a town on the coast

explanation.surface: A French writer has written about a river near Aquitaine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Written about' seems to mean wrote on a topic, but it wraps the author's name around the river letter and a word meaning close to (as a town 'on' the coast).
explanation.definitionFit: The Gironde is a French department that was part of the Aquitaine region.

clue.text: Tenderloin offered at a cheaper price?

explanation.surface: A butcher's cut of beef, priced to beat the competition.
explanation.definitionFit: In British butchery this is the beef fillet cut from below the sirloin; as a verb it means selling below a rival's price.

clue.text: Imagine the human form

explanation.surface: Picture a person's body.
explanation.definitionFit: To figure is informal for to suppose or picture; a figure is also the shape of a person's body.

clue.text: Flourish or flourished, overcoming trouble

indicators.note: overcoming means on top of, so in this down entry the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: fl. is the abbreviation for flourished, used of when a person was active
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Someone thrives, or once thrived, despite getting over hardship.
explanation.walkthrough: fl. (floruit, flourished) is used in reference books for the period when someone was active.
explanation.definitionFit: To flail is to wave the arms about wildly, a wild brandishing motion.

clue.text: Maybe hotel most of day is overwhelmed by air-conditioning noise

indicators.note: is overwhelmed by means swamped by something around it, so the shortened day goes inside the noise word

parts.note: commotion is a noisy disturbance

indicators.note: most of means all but the end, so the last letter of day goes

parts.note: taken as the word day

explanation.surface: Perhaps a hotel where daytime is drowned out by the din of the air-conditioning.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most of' trims day to DA; 'is overwhelmed by' buries it inside the word for noise, after the air-conditioning letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A hotel is one example of lodging, a place to stay.

clue.text: Bed cover from which article's slipped out

indicators.note: slipped out means escaped, so the article letter leaves the cover word

parts.note: a coat is a covering, as a coat of paint
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A bedspread from which an item has slid off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bed cover' reads as one phrase, a duvet, but 'Bed' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cot is a small bed, especially a child's.

clue.text: Metal objects wife placed in safe

indicators.note: placed in means put inside, so the wife letter goes into the safe word

parts.note: peter is old criminal slang for a safe

explanation.surface: Metal items belonging to a wife are locked in a safe.
explanation.walkthrough: PETER is old thieves' slang for a safe, a crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: The tin alloy also names the collection of plates and tankards made from it.

clue.text: Delicate design of most of folder, square

indicators.note: most of means all but the end, so the last letter of the folder word goes

parts.note: a file is a folder for papers
to square with something is to agree with it

explanation.surface: An intricate pattern on most of a folder, squared off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' looks like a shape but it is the verb meaning to tally, AGREE.
explanation.definitionFit: Filagree, a variant spelling of filigree, is ornamental openwork of fine wire.
